questions.question: In a Transformer decoder block used for autoregressive language modeling, what is the primary purpose of applying a causal mask within the self-attention module?
questions.choice_A: To prevent each token from attending to future positions, enforcing left-to-right factorization of the joint distribution
questions.choice_B: To reduce the number of attention heads without hurting accuracy
questions.choice_C: To normalize the attention scores so they sum to one
questions.choice_D: To allow bidirectional context during training but not during inference

questions.question: Why are multiple attention heads used within a multi-head attention layer?
questions.choice_A: To reduce computational cost by parallelizing queries across GPUs
questions.choice_B: To allow the model to attend to different representation subspaces and capture diverse relational patterns
questions.choice_C: To ensure the softmax temperature differs across heads for stability
questions.choice_D: To eliminate the need for positional encodings

questions.question: Which statement best characterizes the difference between BPE and SentencePiece (Unigram) tokenization for LLMs?
questions.choice_A: BPE is character-based while SentencePiece is purely word-based
questions.choice_B: BPE merges frequent symbol pairs deterministically, whereas Unigram models select a subword vocabulary probabilistically to maximize corpus likelihood
questions.choice_C: BPE requires language-specific rules, while SentencePiece cannot handle multilingual corpora
questions.choice_D: Both require whitespace-delimited input and cannot operate on raw byte streams

questions.question: What is a key implication of the quadratic complexity of standard self-attention with respect to context length $L$?
questions.choice_A: Training time scales linearly with $L$ but memory does not
questions.choice_B: Both compute and memory scale as $\mathcal{O}(L)$, which becomes prohibitive for short sequences
questions.choice_C: Compute and memory scale as $\mathcal{O}(L^2)$ due to the full attention matrix, making very long contexts costly
questions.choice_D: The complexity is dominated by feed-forward layers, not attention, regardless of $L$

questions.question: In next-token prediction with an autoregressive model, how is the joint probability of a sequence $x_{1:T}$ typically factorized?
questions.choice_A: $p(x_{1:T}) = \prod_{t=1}^T p(x_t \mid x_{<t})$

questions.question: Which decoding strategy tends to produce more diverse outputs at the cost of potential coherence and is controlled by a probability mass threshold?
questions.choice_A: Greedy decoding
questions.choice_B: Nucleus (top-$p$) sampling
questions.choice_C: Beam search with small beam
questions.choice_D: Deterministic top-1 sampling

questions.question: What is the main motivation for tying input and output token embeddings in language models?
questions.choice_A: It reduces the number of attention heads needed for convergence
questions.choice_B: It removes the need for positional encodings
questions.choice_C: It shares parameters between the embedding and softmax weight matrix, improving parameter efficiency and sometimes generalization
questions.choice_D: It prevents exposure bias during training

questions.question: How does key-value (KV) caching accelerate autoregressive decoding at inference time?
questions.choice_A: By predicting multiple tokens in parallel without changing the architecture
questions.choice_B: By reusing computed key and value projections from past tokens so each new step performs attention only against cached states
questions.choice_C: By approximating softmax with a linear function
questions.choice_D: By removing the feed-forward network from every other layer

questions.question: What is a core difference between absolute sinusoidal positional encodings and relative/rotary positional encodings (e.g., RoPE)?
questions.choice_A: Absolute encodings enable extrapolation to longer contexts better than relative encodings
questions.choice_B: Relative/rotary encodings represent positions through pairwise offsets, preserving distance information and often generalizing better to shifted windows
questions.choice_C: Absolute encodings eliminate the need for attention masking
questions.choice_D: Relative encodings cannot be used in decoder-only models

questions.question: Which statement about vocabulary size in subword tokenization is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Larger vocabularies always reduce training compute
questions.choice_B: Smaller vocabularies always improve perplexity
questions.choice_C: Larger vocabularies reduce sequence length but increase softmax parameter count and compute; smaller vocabularies do the opposite
questions.choice_D: Vocabulary size has negligible impact on model memory footprint

questions.question: What is the "softmax bottleneck" in language modeling?
questions.choice_A: The inability of a single softmax layer to represent certain complex conditional distributions due to its low-rank logit parameterization
questions.choice_B: The instability caused by high temperatures during decoding
questions.choice_C: The slow convergence of softmax cross-entropy loss relative to other losses
questions.choice_D: The memory overhead of storing logits before softmax

questions.question: In teacher-forced training for next-token prediction, what is a known drawback that can affect generation quality at inference?
questions.choice_A: The model learns to ignore attention due to label smoothing
questions.choice_B: Exposure bias: the model is only trained on gold prefixes, but must condition on its own (possibly erroneous) outputs at inference
questions.choice_C: The loss is non-differentiable with respect to the logits
questions.choice_D: The objective does not factorize over time steps

questions.question: Compared to masked language modeling (MLM) objectives, what is a typical advantage of autoregressive next-token prediction for open-ended generation?
questions.choice_A: Autoregressive models can use bidirectional context at inference
questions.choice_B: Autoregressive training aligns directly with left-to-right generation, simplifying decoding and often improving fluency
questions.choice_C: MLM always yields worse perplexity under the same compute
questions.choice_D: Autoregressive models require no positional encodings

questions.question: What do empirical scaling laws for LLMs generally suggest about optimal allocation of compute between model size and dataset size?
questions.choice_A: Maximize parameters while keeping data fixed for best returns
questions.choice_B: Maximize data while keeping parameters fixed for best returns
questions.choice_C: There is an approximate compute-optimal frontier where increasing model size should be paired with commensurate increases in data to maintain efficient loss improvements
questions.choice_D: Loss improves only with model depth, not width or data

questions.question: Why is layer normalization placement (Pre-LN vs Post-LN) significant in Transformer training?
questions.choice_A: It determines whether attention is causal or bidirectional
questions.choice_B: Pre-LN often stabilizes gradients and enables training at higher learning rates and deeper networks compared to Post-LN
questions.choice_C: Post-LN is always superior due to better test perplexity
questions.choice_D: Layer norm placement only affects inference speed, not training stability

questions.question: Which statement about attention heads and emergent behaviors (e.g., induction heads) is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: All heads learn identical patterns, providing redundancy rather than specialization
questions.choice_B: Some heads specialize in operations like copying or matching repeated substrings, supporting in-context learning phenomena
questions.choice_C: Head specialization only occurs in encoder-only models
questions.choice_D: Specialization is prevented when using rotary positional encodings

questions.question: What is the primary computational benefit of using the feed-forward network (FFN) with an expansion ratio (e.g., 4x) in Transformer blocks?
questions.choice_A: It reduces the number of parameters by sharing weights across layers
questions.choice_B: It provides a powerful token-wise nonlinearity that increases model capacity with compute dominated by dense matmuls that parallelize efficiently
questions.choice_C: It replaces the need for multi-head attention entirely
questions.choice_D: It enables sub-quadratic attention complexity

questions.question: How does adjusting softmax temperature $\tau$ during decoding affect output distributions?
questions.choice_A: Higher $\tau$ sharpens the distribution, increasing determinism
questions.choice_B: Lower $\tau$ increases entropy, promoting diversity
questions.choice_C: Higher $\tau$ flattens the distribution, increasing randomness; lower $\tau$ sharpens it
questions.choice_D: Temperature has no effect when using top-$p$ sampling

questions.question: Which trade-off is most relevant when increasing context length during pretraining?
questions.choice_A: Longer contexts reduce overfitting without affecting compute
questions.choice_B: Longer contexts substantially increase attention compute/memory and may dilute batch diversity unless global tokens or curriculum strategies are used
questions.choice_C: Longer contexts eliminate the need for tokenization entirely
questions.choice_D: Longer contexts always improve downstream performance regardless of task

questions.question: What is a conceptual reason perplexity is used to evaluate language models trained with next-token prediction?
questions.choice_A: Perplexity directly measures factual accuracy on QA tasks
questions.choice_B: Perplexity is invariant to tokenization choices
questions.choice_C: Perplexity is a monotonic transform of average negative log-likelihood, reflecting how well the model predicts held-out tokens
questions.choice_D: Perplexity is unaffected by vocabulary size and sequence length
